title: Broker (Delala) vs Professional Movers in Addis Ababa
excerpt: How delala brokers underquote condo moves in Addis—and what professional movers put in writing: survey, truck class, lift slots, and fixed scope before deposit.
content:
What a delala does

A delala (broker) connects you to a truck and day labor—often via phone or Telegram—without owning the crew or vehicle. The price sounds low because it excludes compound rules, elevator bookings, stair carries, and standby time at the gate. On moving day a different truck may appear, and the number grows while boxes sit on the curb.

What professional movers do differently

Active Movers (and other reputable operators) start with a walkthrough or video survey, name truck class and crew size, and send a written quote before deposit. We register plates with security when you provide management contacts, confirm freight lift slots, and assign a crew lead who stays accountable at both gates.

Common delala surprises in Addis

  • “Stairs extra” or “big truck needed” only after load starts.
  • Truck rejected at condo gate—no insurance letter, wrong plate, no move permit.
  • Hourly meter with no cap while security delays entry.
  • Damage with no declared value or receipt trail.
  • Second trip because volume was never surveyed.

Where brokers hurt most

High-rise condos in Bole, Friendship City, CMC Mikael, and Ayat—management expects one vendor, one elevator block, and ID lists. Kazanchis offices need after-hours freight and labeled IT—brokers rarely plan phases. Historic core moves need small-truck staging—brokers send oversized vehicles that cannot turn.

How to compare quotes fairly

Line up delala cash price against a professional quote that includes blankets, disassembly, and gate coordination. Add your own time, damage risk, and second-trip probability—see DIY vs professional true cost. Published starts (studio from about 17,000 ETB) are on the 2026 cost guide and homepage pricing.

Protect yourself in writing

Insist on company name, scope, payment schedule, and change-order rules—contract red flags · price creep · reliable mover checklist.

When a broker might be acceptable

A few boxes, ground floor, both ends with legal parking, and you accept breakage risk—maybe a pickup and helpers suffice. The moment a freight lift, fridge, or Gotera traffic window enters the job, book professionals with fixed or capped terms—hourly vs fixed.

Ask the broker directly

Who owns the truck? Who pays if a mirror breaks? What happens if security rejects the plate? If answers are vague, book a surveyed professional quote instead—same phone number, written scope.
